title: Domain pack: research and evidence synthesis
description: Rules for evidence-based analysis. Number of sources is explicitly not a quality proxy. See PRD Phase 15.

rules.title: The research question is stated explicitly and is answerable
rules.purpose: Prevent open-ended 'look into this' work from never converging.
rules.requirement: brief.goal states a specific, answerable research question, not a vague topic.
rules.evidence_requirement: The question could, in principle, be answered 'yes/no/uncertain, because...'.

rules.title: Primary sources are preferred over secondary summaries
rules.purpose: Avoid laundering an unreliable summary as if it were the original evidence.
rules.requirement: Where a primary source (official docs, standards, filings, datasets, papers) exists, it is cited in preference to a secondary summary or marketing post.
rules.evidence_requirement: Cited sources are checked against a primary/secondary classification.
rules.source_or_rationale: PRD Phase 1: 'Prefer official product documentation... Avoid treating marketing posts... as authoritative.'

rules.title: Source recency is checked against the research cutoff date
rules.purpose: Prevent stale information from being presented as current.
rules.requirement: Each source's publication or last-updated date is recorded, and staleness relative to the task's needs is called out.

rules.title: Claims are cited next to the claim, not only in a bibliography
rules.purpose: Make it possible to check any single claim without re-deriving the whole source list.
rules.requirement: Each non-obvious factual claim carries its source inline or in an immediately adjacent reference, not only in an end-of-document list.
rules.evidence_requirement: Spot-checking a claim does not require searching the whole bibliography.

rules.title: Contradictory evidence is surfaced, not silently dropped
rules.purpose: Prevent cherry-picking sources that support a preferred conclusion.
rules.requirement: When credible sources disagree, both positions are reported along with why one is judged more reliable, rather than presenting only the preferred one.
rules.evidence_requirement: status.remaining_uncertainty or the deliverable itself names the disagreement.

rules.title: Inference is labeled distinctly from directly observed evidence
rules.purpose: Keep the reader from mistaking the researcher's reasoning for a sourced fact.
rules.requirement: Conclusions drawn by inference (not stated directly by any source) are marked as such, matching the MODEL-EVALUATED or PROPOSED evidence labels rather than VERIFIED.
rules.evidence_requirement: status.verified_facts and status.unverified_claims use evidence_label correctly.

rules.title: Quotation stays within fair-use-scale limits
rules.purpose: Avoid reproducing copyrighted material at length.
rules.requirement: Quoted material from any single source stays short (a sentence or two) and attributed; longer material is summarized in the researcher's own words instead.
rules.evidence_requirement: No extended verbatim reproduction appears in the deliverable.

rules.title: Uncertainty and the search protocol are recorded for reproducibility
rules.purpose: Let another researcher understand what was and was not covered, and redo the search.
rules.requirement: The report states its search strategy (queries/sources tried), what it could not resolve, and the cutoff date of its own knowledge plus the access date of any live sources.
rules.evidence_requirement: These elements are present in the report, not only implied.
rules.source_or_rationale: PRD Phase 15: 'Uncertainty... Reproducibility... Research cutoff date.'
